# opnsense_nginx_security_header (Data Source)

nginx security header sets (**Services ▸ Nginx ▸ Configuration ▸ HTTP(S) ▸ Security Headers**, plugin `os-nginx`).



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) UUID of the nginx security header set.

### Read-Only

- `content_type_options` (Boolean) Don't Sniff Content Type.
- `csp_connect_src_enabled` (Boolean) If checked, this part of the CSP is enabled.
- `csp_connect_src_http_urls` (Set of String) Allow connecting to websockets. You can use wildcards here like wss://*.exmaple.com.
- `csp_connect_src_none` (Boolean) If this checkbox is checked, all other settings for this directive are ignored and everything will be forbidden.
- `csp_default_src_blob` (Boolean) Allows to use blobs as a data source. This usually is content, which is somehow generated in JavaScript.
- `csp_default_src_data_urls` (Boolean) Data URLs are used to embed files into HTML (for example images written directly into the src attribute).
- `csp_default_src_enabled` (Boolean) If checked, this part of the CSP is enabled.
- `csp_default_src_eval` (Boolean) Checking this box allows functions like eval or createFunction in JS, or style attributes for CSS.
- `csp_default_src_filesystem` (Boolean) Enable File System URLs.
- `csp_default_src_http_urls` (Set of String) Allow loading files over HTTP(S) allows downloading of content over other domains or CDNs. You can use wildcards here like https://*.exmaple.com.

- `description` (String) This is only for your reference.
- `enable_csp` (Boolean) If checked, the Content Security Policy (CSP) header is enabled. A detailed configuration is still required via the other tabs of this sheet.
- `referrer` (String) Same Origin: The header will be sent if you stay on the same server using the same protocol (no data leak) No Referrer When Downgrade: Prevents sending a referrer when switching from HTTPS to HTTP Origin, Strict-Origin: Always send the header but no path or query information. Strict Origin additionally suppressed the header on downgrades. (Strict) Origin When Cross Origin: Full Referrer on the same origin, and like (Strict) Origin when cross domain. Unsafe URL: Sends the full URL to all pages. One of `no-referrer`, `no-referrer-when-downgrade`, `same-origin`, `origin`, `strict-origin`, `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `origin-when-cross-origin`, `unsafe-url`.
- `strict_transport_security_include_subdomains` (Boolean) If checked, also subdomains are affected.
- `strict_transport_security_preload` (Boolean) If checked, the preload directive is added. Google maintains an HSTS preload service. By following the guidelines and successfully submitting your domain, browsers will never connect to your domain using an insecure connection. While the service is hosted by Google, all browsers have stated an intent to use (or actually started using) the preload list. However, it is not part of the HSTS specification and should not be treated as official.
- `strict_transport_security_time` (Number) A time in seconds in which the transport security (TLS) should be enforced.
- `xssprotection` (String) Block: The browser should block the response Off: Allow Anything On: The Browser decides how to handle it. One of `1; mode=block`, `0`, `1`.
